taxonomic_note: Accepted species. Native Texas material corresponds to Ilex vomitoria subsp. vomitoria.
look_here_first: Look at leaf size and persistence: yaupon is the small-leaved evergreen holly—tiny leathery elliptic to obovate leaves with low rounded crenate teeth.

project_inclusion.range_basis: 24-county boundary audit 2026-10-14: Hays, Travis qualify; Williamson are out-of-zone and cannot count toward PASS. Prior citation/evidence text preserved in range_audit; third native county not verified.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Purola Preserve's own yaupon record is introduced and is excluded; landscape cultivars are not range evidence.

range_audit.confidence: high for exclusion of counties not in project zone; prior county-locality evidence retained without fresh specimen reinspection
range_audit.reason: Old PASS counted an excluded county. UNRESOLVED is not FAIL or proof of absence; verify a third accepted county before PASS.

best_field_traits: evergreen multi-stemmed shrub or small tree
alternate simple leathery leaves commonly only 1–4 cm long
leaf blades elliptic to obovate, usually blunt or rounded at tip
margins finely crenate with low rounded teeth, not strongly spiny
small white unisexual flowers in axillary clusters; dioecious
female plants produce abundant persistent red drupes
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Within local hollies, tiny evergreen leathery leaves with low rounded teeth are the fastest field separator.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Possumhaw has larger, thinner leaves and is deciduous. American holly has much larger thick leaves with sharp spine-tipped teeth. Japanese holly is an introduced landscape shrub and commonly bears black fruit.
